rules.quote: Avoid referring to a person’s age or an age group if it’s not relevant.
rules.specification: Treat unnecessary age characterisations and irrelevant age-based student labels as cases of the same relevance check. The student guidance supplies alternatives: level of study, ‘students’ or ‘PhD candidates’. It does not establish a blanket prohibition on other educational labels.
rules.violation_condition: An age, age group or age-based description is included even though it is not relevant to the content.
when: Age references are acceptable when age is relevant.
The relevance test also applies to characterising people by age.
For students, use level of study rather than age unless age is relevant.
The term ‘mature-age student’ is acceptable when relevant to the content.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates the relevance test and its student-specific cases; G-4 avoids separate findings for restatements.

rules.quote: When the reference to age comes before a noun, punctuate it with hyphens.
rules.violation_condition: An age expression modifying a following noun is missing a required hyphen.
when: The age expression comes before and modifies a noun.
The instruction also applies when the age is written in words at the beginning of a sentence.
rules.why: G-1 treats the introductory style heading as a section and marks its independently checkable child instruction.

rules.quote: Unless the age reference begins a sentence, use numerals.
rules.violation_condition: An age reference that does not begin a sentence is written in words rather than numerals.
when: The age reference does not begin the sentence.
An age reference beginning a sentence is exempt from this numeral requirement.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the sentence-initial exception with the numeral rule rather than creating a second rule.

covers.quote: Standalone words in everyday use, like ‘old’ and ‘young’, can carry bias or unintended subtext.

rules.quote: Words that carry stereotypes, for example ‘elderly’, are not acceptable.
rules.specification: ‘Elderly’ is explicitly identified as unacceptable. Other words require a contextual judgement about stereotyping; the preceding sentence does not categorically prohibit every use of ‘old’ or ‘young’.
rules.violation_condition: Language describing people by age carries an age stereotype, including use of ‘elderly’ as an age label.
when: The wording describes people or groups by age.
The possibility that ‘old’ or ‘young’ carries bias is not, by itself, a blanket prohibition on those words.
rules.why: G-1 leaves the respectful-language umbrella as a section; this sentence states a distinct prohibition on stereotyping.

rules.violation_condition: ‘Junior’ or ‘juniors’ is used as a generic age-group label for young people rather than a neutral age term.
